statement: Qur'an 15:94: proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists.

When 26:214 was revealed he climbed Safa, called the clans, asked whether they would believe him about cavalry in the valley; they affirmed his truthfulness; he said he was a warner; Abu Lahab cursed him.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked against both narrations.

statement: Abu Hurayrah: when the verse was revealed he addressed Quraysh, Banu Abd Manaf, Safiyyah and Fatimah, saying he could not avail them before Allah.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. The narration also names al-Abbas in other routes.

statement: They called him a poet, a soothsayer and possessed.
Qur'an 41:26: do not listen to this Qur'an and make noise during it.
Abu Talib did not accept Islam but protected him; Ibn Mas'ud: Allah protected the Messenger of Allah through his uncle Abu Talib.
notes: Ibn Majah 150 graded hasan (al-Albani: hasan sahih); machine-checked.

statement: Leaders of Quraysh went to Abu Talib more than once to have him restrain or surrender his nephew; he did not.
The report 'if they placed the sun in my right hand and the moon in my left' has a weak chain.
notes: Editorial statement. Graded da'if by al-Albani (Silsilah ad-Da'ifah 909, from memory). A different wording is graded hasan by some; reviewer to decide whether to narrate that wording instead.

statement: Utbah ibn Rabi'ah offered wealth, leadership and kingship; the Prophet recited from Surah Fussilat; Utbah advised Quraysh to leave him alone.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq; some routes graded hasan. Narrated as a report, in indirect speech.
